summary: Read-only audit, node1, 2026-11-21. Read CLAUDE.md, lean-egf/docs/CAMPAIGN.md, kb 0006 (lean-causal) and 0015 (lean-egf), the roadmap block T-egf-universality-ergodic (papers/egf/programme/roadmap.toml:101-112), correction C-29 (papers/egf/programme/corrections.toml:461-471), main.tex:216-222, 238, 246-278, 690-705 and 775-804, the ledger row and curation row of theo:universality_true, the follow-up's body/04_universality.tex:1-45, the REPORT and all 1783 lines of the file. The statements are correct. The headline pair is right: EGF.universality_of_ergodic has the conclusion of EGF.main_universality word for word (checked with #check on both), and necessity holds for every Markov pi and finite lambda. The label is not marked, the row is 'partial' and the one added hypothesis (lamHat finite) is disclosed. The build is clean and the axioms are standard. There are no name collisions, the provenance comments are exact and the scope is clean. Three minor points, all wording: (1) the REPORT's finding against main.tex:697/702 depends on the two witnesses not being summably L2-mixing. That is true, but nothing proves it and the REPORT does not say so. (2) The findings that main.tex:238 is 'right' and main.tex:271 is 'true' hold only when ergodicity is read as lambda-ergodicity for a finite invariant lamHat ~ lambda, which is not def:egf's topological ergodicity. (3) SCOPE calls 'the Markov.* block' a verbatim port, but four EGF.Markov declarations are original.

labels.label: theo:universality_true
labels.notes: Not marked: grep finds no **`theo:` mark anywhere in the file. The label is written `theo:universality_true` — `main.tex:775` at character 336. The strict mark stays with EGF.main_universality, as dispatched. Against the PRINTED statement: EGF.universality_of_ergodic (l.1328) assumes [IsFiniteMeasure lam] (the standing finite lambda of main.tex:161, as in main_universality), [IsMarkovKernel pi], and lamHat with [IsFiniteMeasure lamHat], lamHat.bind pi = lamHat, lamHat << lam, lam << lamHat and IsKernelErgodic pi lamHat. It takes probabilities Finit, Fterm << lam with no L2 densities and any eps > 0. It drops Polish, summable mixing and the L2 densities. It adds that lamHat is finite. That addition is disclosed in the checklist (l.57), in SCOPE (l.68-70) and in REPORT.hypotheses as 'strengthened', so 'partial' is the right status. The conclusion, printed by #check next to EGF.main_universality, is identical: exists fout >= 0, bounded, MemLp 2 lam, initialError + terminalError (univ) < eps. EGF.isUniversalPolicy_of_ergodic is that statement folded into EGF.IsUniversalPolicy (EGF/UniversalFamily.lean:113, whose body is main_universality's conclusion quantified over Finit, Fterm, eps). Under the Walters reading that includes lambda pi = lambda (the curation row's second finding), lamHat := lam is admissible and universality_of_ergodic covers the printed statement with mixing dropped. That is not claimed, and it does not affect the status. Against C-29's corrected text (corrections.toml:468) it is Lean >= corrected in full. Read hypothesis by hypothesis, the family and iff forms match their docstrings: universal_iff_ergodic (l.1629), universality_of_ergodic_family (l.1643, which is EGF.universality of EGF/UniversalFamily.lean:287 with IsSummablyL2Mixing replaced by finite invariant lamHat ~ lam plus IsKernelErgodic), not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_not_ergodic (l.1658: every member has policy pi and an outflow << lam), and isUniversalFamilyEps_fixedPolicyFamily_iff (l.1672, with the strict fixedPolicyFamily = {pi} x L2_+(lam)).

checks.IsKernelErgodic: l.764: ∀ A measurable, (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, π x A = 𝟙_A x) → μ A = 0 ∨ μ Aᶜ = 0. This is the standard invariant-set notion for a Markov kernel relative to a measure, and for an invariant μ it is the usual one. For a deterministic kernel it is equivalent to Mathlib's (quasi-)ergodicity, since δ_{Φx}(A) = 𝟙_{Φ⁻¹A}(x). Calling it 'Walters' sense' is a fair gloss: Walters defines it for maps. It is not trivially satisfied (the auditor's probe: Kernel.id on (Bool, uniform) fails it). isKernelErgodic_congr (l.768) is exactly what it claims. Mutual absolute continuity carries the a.e. hypothesis from ν to μ through μ ≪ ν and the null/conull conclusion back through ν ≪ μ. The inhabitants are correctly hypothesized. isKernelErgodic_deterministic_of_quasiErgodic and isKernelErgodic_deterministic go from Mathlib's QuasiErgodic or Ergodic to IsKernelErgodic, the latter also giving μ.bind = μ. IsEGFPolicy.isKernelErgodic needs weights > 0 everywhere and every A with Φᵢ⁻¹A =ᵐ A for all i null or conull, with no invariance. That is right: with positive weights, π x A = 𝟙_A x a.e. forces every move to stay in A or in Aᶜ. isKernelErgodic_egfKernel_uniform needs 0 < p, measurable and μ-preserving moves, and the same common-invariant-set clause. It needs no finiteness of μ, which is weaker than the roadmap's 'finite μ'.
checks.sufficiency_route: No hidden strength. exists_tvMass_cesaro_lt_of_ergodic (l.1058) takes a finite invariant ergodic lamHat, μ₀, μ₁ ≤ K·lamHat and equal masses, and gives some N ≥ 1 with ‖Σ_{t<N}(μ₀−μ₁)πᵗ‖_TV < Nη. tvMass_construction_cesaro (l.1230) takes R with Rπ = R dominating the partial sums of μ₁. Markov.ae_eq_const_of_densityAction_eq (l.915) takes a finite invariant ergodic ν and a measurable integrable z with P z = z a.e., and gives z a.e. constant. That is the classical fact, and the proof goes through the invariant density (z − c)⁺. universality_of_ergodic discharges every one of these hypotheses from its own: truncation (EGF.exists_truncation, which is where lamHat finite is consumed), R = N K lamHat, and equal masses from the two probabilities.
checks.necessity: not_universal_of_not_ergodic (l.1570) assumes only [IsFiniteMeasure lam] and [IsMarkovKernel π], so the claim 'no invariant measure' is true. The instance Finit = lam.withDensity(𝟙_A (lam A)⁻¹) and Fterm = lam.withDensity(𝟙_{Aᶜ} (lam Aᶜ)⁻¹) gives probabilities ≪ lam. It meets the bounded-density clause in the exact format of IsUniversalFamilyEps (∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ᵐ s ∂lam, rnDeriv ≤ C, with C = ((lam A)⁻¹).toNNReal, finite because lam A ≠ 0). IsUniversalPolicy itself has no such clause. For every finite Fout ≪ lam the defect is ≥ 2 (two_le_errors_of_invariant_set: (Fout π)(A) = Fout(A) on the a.e.-invariant A, mass ≥ 1 on A and on Aᶜ). 'Invariant' is the same predicate IsKernelErgodic in both halves: relative to lam for necessity and to lamHat for sufficiency, joined by isKernelErgodic_congr in universal_iff_ergodic and isUniversalFamilyEps_fixedPolicyFamily_iff. The family converse applies hU with the roles μ = Fterm and ν = Finit, consistent with IsUniversalFamilyEps's initialError … ν μ.
checks.mixing_implies_ergodic: isKernelErgodic_of_tendsto (l.1697) takes an invariant lamHat ~ lam, not necessarily finite, with γ₀ ≠ ∞ and γₙ → 0, and gives IsKernelErgodic π lamHat. It goes through the strict main_universality_of_tendsto and necessity. isKernelErgodic_of_isSummablyL2Mixing (l.1710) gives IsKernelErgodic π lam. Both read def:summably_mixing through EGF.Defs' mixingCoeff and transfer (OQ-47's taken reading: φπⁿ = d((φλ)πⁿ)/dλ, H normalised in L²(λ) with λ-mean zero). REPORT.corrections and SCOPE (l.70-72) say this, and every other theorem of the file is independent of OQ-47.
checks.counterexamples: Both are genuinely universal in the sense of IsUniversalPolicy, which is kernel-checked with standard axioms. isUniversalPolicy_addCircle: AddCircle T with volume and the kernel y ↦ δ_{a+y}, under addOrderOf a = 0 (satisfiable), with Mathlib's AddCircle.ergodic_add_left. Swap.isUniversalPolicy_policy: EGF.Swap.flow.policy on (Bool, EGF.Coin.lam). That they are NOT summably L²-mixing is not proved anywhere. For the swap the docstring (l.1774-1776) says so and points to T-egf-mixing-criteria. For the circle translation nothing in the file, the REPORT or any roadmap target proves or plans it, and the section header (l.1715) and the docstring table (l.44) call it 'non-mixing'. The claim is true, by my check by hand. Both maps are unitary on L²(λ), so transfer = φ∘(shift⁻ⁿ) and ∫(φπⁿ)² dλ̂ = γ₀ > 0 for every n. Every invariant λ̂ ~ λ is cλ with c ∈ (0, ∞]: for the circle by ergodicity on the σ-finite part, with an infinite part giving γₙ = ∞; for Bool by swap symmetry. So the findings are true as mathematics. They are worded as if fully anchored (minor finding 1). On main.tex:690-705: l.697 ('the technical assumption of L²-mixing summability needed for universality') and l.702 ('essential to ensure universality') are false when read as claims of necessity, which is their natural reading. Under C-29 with either witness they contradict the paper. l.698 ('two transformations are sufficient') is not claimed false. The REPORT sharpens it, correctly, to one map on the circle. Its gloss on the parenthesis of l.697 (a random translation on T^d is a.s. ergodic, hence a universal policy by C-29) is true and is hedged as formalized only for d = 1. On l.271: the REPORT's 'is true' needs a finite invariant λ̂ ~ λ, because von Neumann acts on L²(λ̂) (minor finding 2). The follow-up finding (04_universality.tex:27, 'Universality then does need mixing') is hedged correctly. It is read in the forward setting the follow-up's own next paragraph names, with p = 1. In that reading the claim stands, and the follow-up's own l.41 'sufficient and not necessary' agrees. The L^p (p > 1) form and the literal frozen-backward setting are disclosed as not formalized.

findings.what: The finding that main.tex:697 and :702 are false relies on both witnesses (the circle translation and the swap) not being summably L2-mixing. The REPORT asserts this ('an isometry, which does not mix') but it is proved nowhere. For the swap the REPORT notes and the Lean docstring defer it to T-egf-mixing-criteria. For the circle no target plans it. The assertion is true (each map is unitary on L2(lambda), so gamma_n = gamma_0 > 0 for every invariant lamHat ~ lambda). The finding goes to the author as a fact, and its anchors prove only universality.
findings.fix: In the finding, add: 'non-mixing of the witnesses not formalized here (gamma_n = gamma_0 > 0, both maps being unitary on L2(lambda); the swap's is T-egf-mixing-criteria's EGF.Swap.not_isSummablyL2Mixing)'. Also say that l.697/l.702 are read as claims of necessity. Either qualify the docstring's 'non-mixing universal policies' (l.44, l.1715) the same way, or prove the circle case (transfer = translation, so ∫(φπⁿ)² dlamHat = ∫φ² dlamHat). Keep C-29's l.697-702 clause off 'proved' until one witness's non-mixing is in Lean, or word it as resting on that elementary check.

findings.what: Both findings call the paper's sentence right or true without its reading. C-29 needs lambda-ergodicity of pi for a finite invariant lamHat ~ lambda. The 'Ergodicity' of l.238 follows def:egf (main.tex:221): topological ergodicity of the group generated by the moves (OQ-48, C-26). In general that does not imply lambda-ergodicity (classically, minimal non-ergodic diffeomorphisms of T^2 exist; not formalized). C-29's own necessity half shows that a topologically ergodic EGF whose policy is not lambda-ergodic is not universal. So l.238 is right in its eps form (probabilities with bounded densities, C-18/C-19) only under the measure-theoretic reading. Likewise, l.271's Cesaro convergence is von Neumann on L2(lamHat) and holds given a finite invariant lamHat. The parenthesis on positive non-uniform weights (EGF.IsEGFPolicy.isKernelErgodic) gives ergodicity but not the invariant measure that universality_of_ergodic also needs.
findings.fix: Word findings[6] as: 'right in its eps form when Ergodicity is read as lambda-ergodicity of the policy with a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda (e.g. uniform weights and measure-preserving moves without a common a.e.-invariant set, EGF.isKernelErgodic_egfKernel_uniform); under def:egf's topological ergodicity (OQ-48) it does not follow from C-29'. Add 'given a finite invariant lamHat ~ lambda' to findings[3]. Mirror both qualifications in C-29's finding text when it is adopted.
